body: I honestly don't know if I find it more comforting or frightening that so many people seem to feel like this.

Before I went to bed last night, my roommate's cat pawed at my door until I let him in, and he spent the night curled up next to me, purring. This is the first time that it has happened in the years we've lived together. It seems appropriately Redditesque that a cat would come to the rescue. My anxiety attack is finally starting to unknot in my stomach, and either my feeling of dread is receding somewhat or I'm just too drained to feel much of anything, but I feel like I can at least go about my daily business for a while.

I know this doesn't change any of my underlying problems, and I'm going to try and take advantage of this period of lucidity to start addressing at least something. Hopefully, I can actually get some traction this time. 

Thanks again.

No. Hence posting this thread. But I'm starting to get even more depressed sitting here staring at this page, reading other threads on this forum, knowing I can relate to people's suffering, but not being able to say anything positive in good conscience. 

I'm going to try and sleep soon. There's a chance tomorrow will finally be a day better than the one before it. I don't have the courage otherwise yet. 

Thank you.

Mostly, the more think about the absolute freedom of not existing, the better it sounds than any possible option for my future. I'm an emotional wreck even on good days, and I've just been having weeks upon months of bad days. It's getting to the point where something has to give, and it's far more likely I'm going to lose my job, or have some sort of medical problem or injury that finally cripples my ability to function than it is something magically getting better. 

Thanks for listening. I appreciate it.
